t: You're standing at Clifford's Inn, which is now a mansion block but was once an Inn of Chancery, sitting between Fetter Lane and Clifford's Inn Passage. The Inn was founded in 1344 and refounded in 1668. It was the first Inn of Chancery to be founded and the last to be demolished. Most of it came down in 1934, but a gateway survives. The name comes from Robert de Clifford, the first Baron de Clifford, a soldier who became Lord Warden of the Marches, defending the border with Scotland.
